text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired for gpu-node-17: heartbeat lost, kubelet status=NotReady, metric: host_ping=0. Link: https://pagerduty.example/PD-7890 :rotating_light:

pagerduty: Incident PD-7890 created (severity: high). Escalation policy: infra-oncall -> infra-lead. Page sent to: maria, sanjay.

maria: acked. I'm on it, pulling node details now.

sanjay: oncall here, thanks. any customer-facing impact?

maria: looking at console output from the host, serial shows repeated NVMe errors then watchdog. Not seeing a clean kernel oops yet.

maria: `kubectl get nodes gpu-node-17 -o wide` shows Ready=NotReady, lastTransition=~3m ago. Pods evicted automatically? some still on node.

jen: @maria if we need to drain, we can preemptively move critical workloads to gpu-pool-standby. I can run drains.

maria: doing `kubectl cordon gpu-node-17` now.

maria: cordoned. starting `kubectl drain gpu-node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` to migrate pods. Will watch for stuck pods (ML batch jobs).

ops-bot: autoscaler note: cluster autoscaler will not scale while node is cordoned; manual capacity increase may be required for heavy load.

kai: Observability: we're seeing a spike in inference errors (502/504) from a handful of hosts pinned to gpu-node-17; routing fallback applied for new requests. Old in-flight streams may have dropped.

maria: drain completed but 2 pods stuck in Terminating (CSI detach waiting). killing them with `kubectl delete pod <pod> --grace-period=0 --force`.

sanjay: I'll open a quick support ticket to notify customers in case their nightly batch jobs were affected. tagging growth for comms.

maria: pulled kernel ring buffer via serial: pattern: `nvme 0: failed command` repeated then `watchdog: BUG: soft lockup` then connection loss. suspect hardware NVMe flake leading to host-level lock.

jen: can we safely migrate any long-running model shards? If not, fallback to lower-capacity replicas in other racks.

maria: starting live migration for model-shard pods where possible. For stateful training jobs we need manual retry.

incident-bot: Escalation timer fired, paging infra-lead (jen).

jen: here. I'll take lead for mitigation. Maria continue with host logs and serial. Kai keep an eye on customer error rates and throttles. SRE run a node reboot remote?

maria: requested remote power cycle via BMC. BMC reports host unreachable for ~30s then accepted a power-cycle job. Initiated soft reboot.

ops-bot: reminder: soft reboot may leave NVMe in bad state; if reboot fails, plan for power-cycle + storage controller reseat.

maria: host came back but kubelet failed to register: kubelet logs show `failed to start Kubelet: device-mapper: unreachable NVMe devices`, kubelet restarted loop.

sanjay: handing off paging and oncall to jen — I'm stepping out for 20m.

jen: ack handoff. I'll coordinate with hardware ops for a physical inspection if remote power cycle doesn't stabilize. Maria, can you capture `dmesg` + `journalctl -u kubelet -b` and upload to the incident artifact bucket?

maria: uploading logs -> s3://redwood-incidents/PD-7890/gpu-node-17/ (uploaded). Also pasted a trimmed `dmesg` snippet in the thread.

jen: good. customer impact: Kai says ~0.8% of requests retried and routed; no major outage but degraded for some tenants. We should notify support-run and standby on-call. Kai, please prepare a short summary for customer comms: what's affected, mitigation steps, ETA.

kai: summary draft: "We observed intermittent GPU host connectivity issues affecting a subset of inference requests. Traffic rerouted to healthy hosts; some in-flight requests failed and were retried. We're mitigating and investigating hardware NVMe instability; next update in 30 minutes."

jen: looks good. schedule: immediate mitigation = cordon/drain + retries; mid-term = hardware inspection and potential NVMe replacement; long-term = add node-level NVMe checks to preflight.

incident-bot: PD-7890 status -> acknowledged by maria, escalated to jen, oncall change: sanjay -> jen.

jen: I'll stay on this until we have a stable node state or a hardware swap scheduled. Maria, once ops confirms hardware ticket, hand off to hardware oncall with the logs and the S3 path.

maria: hardware ticket created #HW-3344 assigned to oncall-tech. included S3 logs and BMC trace.

jen: thanks. handoff at 12:08 UTC to hardware. leaving the incident channel open. If node recovers and kubelet stays healthy for 10min, we'll mark as mitigated but keep monitoring.

ops-bot: monitoring: set alert threshold to detect recurrent NVMe errors on other nodes; increase check frequency for next 12h.

maria: final note: no data loss observed for persisted model shards; ephemeral batch workloads that were killed will need resubmission.

jen: 👍 marking active mitigation. next update or final on status in 30m.

pagerduty: PD-7890 -> status: acknowledged, assignees: jen, maria, hardware-oncall.

maria: handing off message: leaving for brief break, jen you're primary.

jen: copy. moving to incident tracking doc -> https://docs.example/incidents/PD-7890. closing pager notifications for non-assignees.

incident-bot: last activity at 2270012450.
